true.x-description: Runs the decision-coverage gate and can block the phase seal if stated decisions were not honored. Recommended when your project has a meaningful decisions record you want enforced.

false.x-description: Disables the decision-coverage gate so phases seal regardless of unresolved decisions. Use this if the gate is too noisy or your project does not track decisions in a way the checker understands.

workflow.context_guard_mode.x-description: Controls how GSD reacts when the executor's context window is running low during a phase. In warn mode it alerts you and recommends pausing; in auto mode it pauses on its own before the next wave; off disables the guard entirely. The guard is heuristic and meant to prevent degraded output from an overstuffed context.

warn.x-description: The orchestrator warns you when context pressure is high and recommends running /gsd-pause-work, but leaves the choice to you. This is the recommended default because it informs you without surprising you with an automatic pause.

auto.x-description: The orchestrator automatically pauses the phase before the next wave when context pressure is high. Use this when you want hands-free protection against degraded output and do not mind the workflow stopping for a handoff.

off.x-description: Disables the context exhaustion guard entirely. Only use this when you have verified the phase fits comfortably and you want to avoid any guard interference, accepting the risk of quality loss if context runs out.

workflow.cross_ai_command.x-description: The shell command GSD uses to run plans through an external AI tool when cross-AI execution is enabled. The plan's task prompt is piped to this command via stdin. If cross-AI execution is on and this is empty, GSD reports an error and asks you to set it. Only fill this in when you have a specific external AI workflow.

workflow.cross_ai_execution.x-description: Enables running certain plans through an external AI command instead of GSD's own executor. Plans marked with cross_ai: true in their frontmatter are then handed off to that external tool, which can be useful for specialized or legacy workflows. Leave this off unless you have deliberately set up an external cross-AI command.

true.x-description: Plans flagged for cross-AI execution are dispatched to the external command set in workflow.cross_ai_command. Enable this only when you have a working external AI integration and plans explicitly marked for it.

false.x-description: Cross-AI execution is disabled and all plans run through GSD's built-in executor. This is the recommended default for normal use.

workflow.cross_ai_timeout.x-description: How long, in seconds, GSD waits for the external cross-AI command to finish a single plan before treating it as timed out. Increase this for large or slow external AI tools; decrease it to fail faster on hung commands. The default of 300 seconds (5 minutes) works for most setups.

workflow.discuss_mode.x-description: Controls what the discuss phase actually does. In discuss mode, GSD asks you interactive questions to clarify scope and approach. In assumptions mode, it instead analyzes the codebase and surfaces the assumptions it detected, without quizzing you. Pick the style that fits how you like to share context.

discuss.x-description: Runs an interactive question-and-answer session to explore the phase's scope, constraints, and preferences. Choose this when you prefer to steer the phase by answering targeted questions, or when the work has many valid tradeoffs.

assumptions.x-description: GSD examines the codebase and reports the assumptions it is making instead of asking you questions. Use this when you would rather review and correct a list of detected assumptions than answer a long Q&A.

workflow.drift_action.x-description: What the codebase drift gate does when the structural-drift threshold (`workflow.drift_threshold`) is exceeded. With `"warn"`, GSD prints an advisory and recommends refreshing the structure map; with `"auto-remap"`, GSD additionally spawns a codebase-mapper agent to regenerate STRUCTURE.md automatically. Choose `"auto-remap"` only if you trust the mapper to refresh structure without manual review.

warn.x-description: Print an advisory when structural drift exceeds the threshold. The default — you decide when to refresh STRUCTURE.md.

auto-remap.x-description: Automatically spawn a codebase-mapper agent to refresh STRUCTURE.md when drift is detected. Convenient, but runs the mapper without a manual review gate.

workflow.human_verify_mode.x-description: Chooses when GSD asks a human to review the work it has done. In mid-flight mode, verification checkpoints happen during the phase so problems are caught early. In end-of-phase mode, all verification happens in one pass at the end. Mid-flight is safer for risky changes; end-of-phase is faster and less interruptive.

end-of-phase.x-description: Verification happens once after the whole phase completes. This keeps execution fast and unbroken, and is fine when you trust the plan and the work is reversible. Problems are caught later, in a single review pass.

mid-flight.x-description: Verification checkpoints happen during the phase so you can catch mistakes early, before later tasks build on top of bad work. Use this on high-risk phases or when a wrong step would be expensive to undo.

workflow.inline_plan_threshold.x-description: Plans with this many tasks or fewer are executed inline by the orchestrator instead of spawning a separate subagent, which avoids the token overhead of launching an agent for a tiny job. Set it to 0 to always spawn subagents, or raise it to inline more small plans. The default of two keeps very cheap plans fast.

workflow.max_discuss_passes.x-description: Limits how many rounds of questions GSD will go through in the discuss phase before it stops and moves on. A higher number allows a deeper, more thorough exploration of the phase, while a lower number keeps the discussion short. The default of three is usually enough to surface the key issues without fatigue.

workflow.mvp_mode.x-description: Persists the MVP flag in config so every phase is framed as a vertical slice one user-visible capability at a time (UI, then API, then database) without needing the --mvp flag on each CLI command. When on, the planner, executor, verifier, and discovery surfaces all treat phases this way. Use it when your whole milestone is structured as thin end-to-end slices.

true.x-description: Defaults every phase to MVP framing, building one thin vertical slice at a time. Ideal when your milestone is a sequence of small, demonstrable increments that each go all the way through the stack.

false.x-description: Phases are not assumed to be MVP slices unless you pass --mvp on the command line. This is the better default for phases that naturally span only one layer, like a pure database migration or a standalone API.

workflow.node_repair.x-description: Lets GSD automatically retry and fix a failed plan task (a node) before reporting the failure to you. When on, the executor diagnoses the failure and attempts corrective edits, which can save you from stepping in on routine compilation errors, test flakiness, or small logic mistakes. Turn it off if you want to inspect and fix every failure yourself.

true.x-description: Enables automatic repair of failed tasks, giving the executor a chance to recover from common, fixable problems without stopping the phase. Recommended for most work because it reduces the number of trivial failures that interrupt your flow.

false.x-description: Disables automatic repair, so any failed task stops the phase and is handed to you. Use this when you want full control over how failures are resolved, or when automatic retries could mask a deeper design problem.

workflow.node_repair_budget.x-description: Sets how many times GSD may automatically retry a single failed task before it gives up and escalates the failure to you. A higher budget can recover from flaky or multi-step problems, but it also means a truly stuck task will waste more time before you see it. The default of two strikes a balance between resilience and quick escalation.

workflow.plan_bounce.x-description: Enables an external plan-bounce validation step against each generated PLAN.md. When on, every plan is passed through the command set in `workflow.plan_bounce_script`, and a non-zero exit code blocks the workflow from proceeding. This lets you enforce custom structural or policy rules on plans (required sections, estimation limits, banned approaches) before execution begins.

true.x-description: Enable plan-bounce validation. Each PLAN.md is piped through `workflow.plan_bounce_script`, and the workflow blocks on a failing script. Requires `plan_bounce_script` to be set.

false.x-description: Skip external plan validation. Plans proceed directly to review/execution. This is the default because most projects do not have a custom validation script.

workflow.plan_bounce_passes.x-description: How many iterative plan-bounce passes GSD runs against a plan. Each pass re-validates the (possibly revised) plan through the bounce script, so a value greater than 1 lets a plan be reworked and re-checked up to this many times before it is finally rejected. Use a higher value when your script produces fixable findings and you want GSD to attempt corrections first.

workflow.plan_bounce_script.x-description: Path to the executable script used for plan-bounce validation when `workflow.plan_bounce` is enabled. GSD runs this script with the path of the PLAN.md file as its first argument and pipes the plan content over stdin; the script must exit 0 for the plan to pass. Set it to null (the default) when you are not using plan-bounce validation.

workflow.plan_check.x-description: Enables a dedicated checker agent that reviews a finished plan for correctness, consistency, and completeness before execution begins. When on, the plan gets a second pair of eyes that can catch missing steps, contradictions, or unsafe approaches. Leave this on for confidence, or turn it off to shave a little time on plans you already trust.

true.x-description: Runs a plan-checker agent that critiques the plan and flags problems before execution starts. Recommended for most phases, especially large or risky ones, because catching a bad plan early is far cheaper than rework later.

false.x-description: Skips the plan-check step entirely so execution begins as soon as the plan is written. Use this only on small, well-understood plans where the overhead of the check is not worth the time.

workflow.plan_chunked.x-description: Enables chunked planning mode. Instead of running one long-lived planner task, GSD splits planning into a short outline task followed by several short per-plan tasks (roughly 3–5 minutes each). Each plan is committed individually, so a crash or interruption does not lose the entire planning session. This is especially helpful on Windows, where long-lived tasks can hang on stdio issues.

true.x-description: Enable chunked planning. Produces many short, individually committed plans. Recommended for long plans, unstable environments, or Windows hosts where long tasks are risky.

false.x-description: Run planning as a single long-lived task. Fewer commits and less overhead for short, straightforward plans.

workflow.plan_review_convergence.x-description: Enables the automated plan→review→replan convergence loop in `/gsd-plan-review-convergence`. When enabled, GSD repeatedly runs plan-phase and an external AI review lane, feeding the review findings back into the planner, until the reviewers raise no further HIGH concerns (up to a bounded number of cycles). This replaces a manual back-and-forth with an automated loop. When disabled, the convergence command exits early with instructions to turn it on.

true.x-description: Enable the automated plan/review convergence loop. GSD keeps planning and reviewing until reviewer concerns converge, saving manual iteration.

false.x-description: Disable convergence. `/gsd-plan-review-convergence` will exit and tell you to enable this first. Default off because convergence consumes multiple review cycles.

workflow.smart_zone_tokens.x-description: Sets the token budget GSD uses to decide whether a phase is large enough to warrant splitting. When a phase's estimate exceeds this number, GSD recommends breaking it into smaller phases. It is an advisory policy default, not a hard limit, so the warning is a nudge to consider splitting rather than a blocker.

workflow.research_before_questions.x-description: Makes GSD do a codebase research pass before it starts the interactive discussion questions for a phase. This gives the agent context so its questions are better targeted and less generic. It adds a little time to the discuss phase but usually yields a much sharper understanding of the work.

true.x-description: Runs a quick research step first so the discussion questions are informed by the actual code and project structure. Use this for unfamiliar codebases or complex phases where generic questions would waste time.

false.x-description: Goes straight to the discussion questions without a research pass. Fine when you already know the codebase well or want to move quickly through a simple, well-understood phase.

workflow.security_block_on.x-description: The minimum open threat severity that will block a phase from advancing. The auditor counts only open threats at or above this severity toward the blocking gate. Raising the bar to `"critical"` means only the most severe findings block progress, while lowering it to `"low"` makes the gate stricter. Set it to `"none"` to disable severity-based blocking entirely (threats are still tracked, they just never block).

critical.x-description: Only critical-severity findings block advancement. Least strict severity gate — useful while triaging a large backlog of legacy findings.

high.x-description: High-severity and critical findings block advancement. The recommended default for most teams.

medium.x-description: Medium, high, and critical findings block advancement. Stricter — adopted once a project wants to treat moderate risks as release blockers.

low.x-description: Low and above block advancement. Very strict — even minor findings must be resolved before the phase can advance.

none.x-description: Severity never blocks advancement. Threats are still tracked, but the gate is effectively disabled. Use when another process owns enforcement.

workflow.skip_discuss.x-description: Skips the discuss phase entirely, moving straight from planning to execution without the usual clarification step. This saves time on trivial or well-understood phases, but you lose the chance to catch misunderstandings early. Only turn this on when the phase's intent is already crystal clear.

true.x-description: Bypasses the discussion phase so the plan goes straight into execution. Use this for small, unambiguous changes where the requirements are obvious and the risk of misunderstanding is low.

false.x-description: Runs the normal discuss phase before planning. This is the recommended default because the discussion often surfaces hidden constraints, saving time and rework later.

workflow.specless_probe_fallback.x-description: Controls what happens when a phase's SPEC is missing its Edge Coverage or Prosections sections. When on (the default), GSD runs a probing pass to discover those predicates and writes them into the plan. When off, the fallback is skipped and a visible marker is emitted so you know the probe was intentionally not run.

true.x-description: Runs an automated probe to recover edge cases and prohibitions when the SPEC does not supply them. Recommended because it keeps incomplete SPECs from silently producing weak plans.

false.x-description: Skips the probe fallback for SPECs without edge/prohibition sections, recording the skip visibly instead. Use this when you want full manual control and would rather fill those sections yourself than let the probe guess.

workflow.subagent_timeout.x-description: Sets the timeout in milliseconds for parallel subagent tasks such as codebase mapping. If a subagent takes longer than this, GSD stops it and reports a timeout. Increase this for very large codebases or slower models; the default of 300000 (5 minutes) fits most projects.

workflow.test_command.x-description: A custom shell command that GSD runs as the regression and test gate. When unset, GSD auto-detects the right command from your Makefile, package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, or pyproject.toml. Set this only when auto-detection picks the wrong command or you need special arguments for a one-shot test run.

workflow.test_gate_timeout.x-description: How long, in seconds, GSD lets the test runner run during the regression gate before aborting it. If tests are stuck in watch or dev mode instead of running once, the run is cut off with a warning. The default is 600 seconds (10 minutes); raise it for slow test suites or lower it to catch stuck runners sooner.

workflow.text_mode.x-description: Switches GSD's interactive prompts from structured AskUserQuestion menus to plain numbered text lists. This is primarily a compatibility and readability option for terminals or environments that cannot render the structured menus. Most users should leave this off.

true.x-description: Uses plain-text numbered lists for questions and choices instead of the richer menu UI. Enable this if your terminal or harness renders the structured menus poorly, or if a screen reader works better with plain text.

false.x-description: Uses GSD's default structured menus for prompts. This is the recommended setting in supported environments because the menus are clearer and easier to navigate.

workflow.use_worktrees.x-description: Runs each parallel executor agent in its own isolated git worktree so concurrent edits do not collide. This is the safe way to get parallelism on a shared branch, but it adds overhead and can complicate merge handling. Turn it off to run sequentially on the main working tree, which is simpler and recommended for solo developers.

true.x-description: Executor agents work in separate git worktrees, keeping concurrent changes isolated. Recommended for parallel execution, though note that a diverged branch may temporarily force sequential runs.

false.x-description: All agents work directly on the main working tree, one at a time. Simpler and recommended when you do not need parallelism or find worktree merges cumbersome.

workflow.verifier.x-description: When true, GSD runs a verifier agent after execution to check that the phase's deliverables match its plan and acceptance criteria. It is one of the core quality gates that catches drift between what was planned and what was built. Keep it on unless you intentionally want no automated post-execution verification.

true.x-description: The verifier runs after execution to validate deliverables against the plan. Recommended as a standard safety net that catches gaps before you move on.

false.x-description: No automated verifier step runs after execution. You lose the automated post-build validation and rely on manual review or other gates.

workflow.worktree_skip_hooks.x-description: Lets executor commits inside worktrees bypass pre-commit hooks when they would otherwise fail or slow things down. By default hooks run on each task commit to catch issues early; this setting opts out of that behavior only where the project explicitly chooses to. Enable it only if your hooks are incompatible with the worktree workflow.

true.x-description: Executor commits skip pre-commit hooks in worktrees. Use this only when your hooks fail in worktree contexts or make execution unbearably slow, accepting that hook-time checks will not run on those commits.

false.x-description: Hooks run normally on executor commits. This is the recommended default because it preserves your project's quality checks on every introducing commit.

claude_orchestration.enabled.x-description: Master toggle for the Claude orchestration capability, which is off by default and currently in BETA. When true, it unlocks the Workflow-tool execution backend and the ultraplan plan-offload surface, changing how execute-phase dispatches work. When false, loop behavior is identical to a non-Claude runtime that uses inline or manual dispatch.

true.x-description: Enables the Claude orchestration capability and its Workflow/ultraplan dispatch surfaces. Intended for Claude runtimes that have the Agent SDK and Workflow tool available; behavior falls back to inline if requirements are not met.

false.x-description: The orchestration capability is inert. Execution uses the standard inline/manual dispatch path as if the capability did not exist. This is the safe default.

claude_orchestration.execution_backend.x-description: Chooses which execute-phase dispatch backend to use when the Claude orchestration capability is enabled. 'auto' picks the Workflow backend only when the runtime, Workflow tool, and minimum Agent SDK version all line up, otherwise falling back to inline. The other two modes force a specific backend, still failing closed to inline if requirements are not met.

auto.x-description: The default. GSD uses the Workflow backend only when it is actually available and the Agent SDK meets the minimum version; otherwise it silently falls back to inline. Best for most users.

workflow.x-description: Forces the Workflow-tool dispatch backend. If the Workflow tool is missing or the Agent SDK is below claude_orchestration.min_agent_sdk_version, it fails closed to inline. Use this when you explicitly want Workflow-style dispatch.

inline.x-description: Forces the traditional one-agent-per-message inline dispatch, ignoring tool availability entirely. Use this to get the pre-orchestration behavior even on a capable Claude runtime.

claude_orchestration.min_agent_sdk_versi.x-description: The minimum Anthropic Agent SDK version required to activate the Workflow backend when execution_backend is 'auto'. It defaults to the release that introduced the Workflow tool. Raise this to pin a higher floor; any runtime reporting an older or unknown SDK version falls back to inline dispatch.

external_job.enabled.x-description: Master toggle for the async external-job producer capability, which lets an executor submit long-running work to an external scheduler instead of running it inline. The core loop always consumes job manifests, but it never writes a new manifest unless this is true. Keep it false unless you are integrating with a cluster scheduler.

true.x-description: Enables the external-job producer so executors can write job manifests for an external scheduler (e.g., SLURM) to pick up. The consuming side is always active, but new jobs are only produced when this is on.

false.x-description: No external job manifests are ever written. Any work is dispatched inline through the normal executor path, with no scheduler involvement.

external_job.backend.x-description: Selects which scheduler backend the external-job capability targets. SLURM is the first and currently only supported adapter; the field exists as a pluggability seam for future backends like LSF, PBS, or Kubernetes batch. GSD core never interprets this value directly — the adapter does.

slurm.x-description: Use the SLURM scheduler adapter to submit and poll external jobs. This is the only currently supported backend, so leave it as slurm unless a future GSD release documents additional options.

external_job.artifact_dir.x-description: Root directory for per-job artifact folders, into which the scheduler adapter writes outputs such as Artifacts/jobs/<jobid>/. It avoids hardcoding cluster- or project-specific log paths in GSD itself. Override with the GSD_EXTERNAL_JOB_ARTIFACT_DIR environment variable if you need a different location at runtime.

external_job.poll_timeout_ms.x-description: Hard timeout in milliseconds for the scheduler poll subprocess (for example squeue, with a sacct fallback). It bounds how long GSD waits for a status query to return. The default is 15000 ms. Increase it if your scheduler's query commands are slow under load.

external_job.submit_timeout_ms.x-description: Hard timeout in milliseconds for the scheduler submit subprocess (for example sbatch). It bounds how long GSD waits for a job submission command to complete. The default is 30000 ms. Increase it if your cluster's submission step is slow during bursts.

graphify.enabled.x-description: Enables the graphify knowledge-graph command and skill, which builds a structured graph of your codebase's semantic relationships under .planning/graphs/. When true, GSD can build, query, and diff a graph of modules, decisions, and dependencies that planning and research runs use to understand the project. It requires the external graphify tool to be installed.

true.x-description: Graphify commands become available and GSD will build/query a knowledge graph of your codebase. Install graphify first (uv pip install graphifyy && graphify install), otherwise builds will fail.

false.x-description: The graphify capability is inert. No graph is built or queried, and planning relies on other sources of structural context.

intel.enabled.x-description: Enables the queryable codebase intelligence system under .planning/intel/. When true, the /gsd-map-codebase --query command builds and queries a JSON index of your codebase so later planning and research runs can answer structured questions about your project's structure. Keep it false unless you want that index built and maintained.

true.x-description: Activates the intel command and its JSON code-intelligence index, letting you and GSD agents query codebase structure. Adds a build/index step, so enable it when structured codebase queries are worth the overhead.

false.x-description: No codebase intelligence index is built or queried. Codebase insights come only from direct file reads and mapping, with no separate queryable store.

mempalace.enabled.x-description: Master toggle for the MemPalace long-term memory capability. When true, GSD maintains a searchable memory palace that stores decisions, patterns, artifacts, and diary entries across your phases, so future planning runs can recall context from earlier work. Keep this false unless you want GSD to invest time writing and recalling from a separate memory store alongside your regular planning files.

true.x-description: Activates the full MemPalace capability: recall injections at discuss/plan time, artifact filing, knowledge-graph mirroring, diary entries, and any optional hooks you enable below. Each sub-feature still respects its own on/off toggle, so you can turn the palace on globally and disable individual behaviors.

false.x-description: MemPalace does nothing. GSD behaves exactly as if the memory capability does not exist — no recall, no artifact capture, no diary writes. Use this if you rely only on the native .planning/graphs/ folder and want the smallest possible footprint.

mempalace.wing.x-description: Names the MemPalace wing this project writes to and reads from. A wing is an isolated memory namespace, so different projects or contexts can keep separate palaces. When left empty, GSD derives a sensible wing name from your project_code or project directory, which is usually what you want for a single project.

mempalace.recall_on_discuss.x-description: When true, GSD runs a wake-up and search recall step right before the discuss phase begins, injecting relevant memories from the palace into the conversation. This helps surface earlier decisions and patterns while you are scoping and questioning, so you do not re-litigate things the project already settled.

true.x-description: Discuss phase starts by recalling matching memories from the palace and priming the session with them. Recommended for most projects, since it grounds early scoping in what the project already knows.

false.x-description: Discuss phase starts with a blank slate from the palace's perspective. Use this if recall injections are slowing down or distracting from your early discussions.

mempalace.recall_on_plan.x-description: When true, GSD produces a MEMORY-RECALL.md file before planning, summarizing palace memories relevant to the upcoming phase. The planner then consumes this file so plans can build on prior decisions rather than re-deriving them. Turning it off means plans will not receive this prepared recall summary.

true.x-description: A MEMORY-RECALL.md artifact is generated before planning and fed to the planner. Recommended so plans inherit context from earlier phases stored in the palace.

false.x-description: No prepared recall summary is generated; the planner will only see native .planning context. Use this if the recall file is adding noise for a fresh or unrelated phase.

mempalace.capture_artifacts.x-description: When true, GSD files key phase artifacts — CONTEXT, PLAN, SUMMARY, and learnings — into the palace at phase boundaries. This is how the palace accumulates a searchable history of your project over time. Disable it if you do not want phase documents persisted into the memory store.

true.x-description: Phase boundary artifacts are copied into the palace so later recall can surface them. This is the core mechanism that makes the palace useful, so keep it on unless you have a reason not to.

false.x-description: Artifacts are not filed into the palace at phase boundaries. The palace will not grow from your execution, though recall and other behaviors can still run against whatever is already stored.

mempalace.mirror_kg.x-description: When true, decisions and learnings are mirrored into MemPalace's temporal knowledge graph as structured facts. This gives the palace queryable, time-aware relationships (who decided what, when, and why) rather than just a pile of documents. Turn it off if you want artifact storage without the knowledge-graph indexing.

true.x-description: Decision and learning facts are written into the palace's temporal KG, enabling relationship and timeline queries. Recommended if you chose kg_backend or replace memory modes.

false.x-description: No knowledge-graph mirroring happens. The palace keeps artifact files but does not build a queryable graph of decisions and learnings from them.

mempalace.cross_project_tunnels.x-description: When true, GSD proposes or creates cross-wing tunnels after a ship, linking this project's palace to related wings in other projects. Tunnels let one project recall relevant memories from another. This is off by default because it mutates the palace structure based on inferred relationships.

true.x-description: After shipping, GSD may create tunnels between this wing and related wings in other projects, enabling cross-project recall. Enable only if you actively maintain multiple related palaces and want them to share context.

false.x-description: No cross-project tunnels are proposed or created. Each project's palace stays isolated, which is the safer default.

mempalace.diary_journal.x-description: When true, GSD writes a per-agent diary entry at ship time, recording what each agent did and decided during the phase. These diary entries become part of the palace's narrative history and can be recalled later for context. Turn it off if you find the diary entries redundant with your SUMMARY files.

true.x-description: A diary entry is recorded for each agent at ship time, building a narrative history in the palace. Useful for understanding the 'why' behind past execution when you revisit a project later.

false.x-description: No diary entries are written. You lose the per-agent narrative history but keep the shorter phase artifacts and KG facts if those remain enabled.

mempalace.auto_capture_hooks.x-description: Reserved for future use. Eventually this will install MemPalace's native Claude Code stop/precompact hooks to passively capture mid-session context without an explicit phase boundary. It is currently not implemented and enabling it has no effect, so leave it false.

true.x-description: Currently a no-op placeholder. It is reserved for passive mid-session capture hooks that are not yet implemented, so flipping it on today does nothing.

false.x-description: The current default. Passive MemPalace hooks are not installed because the feature is not yet available.

profile-pipeline.enabled.x-description: Enables the developer profiling pipeline commands, which scan prior Claude session history, extract messages, sample conversations, and write an AI-discoverable developer profile. When true, GSD can analyze how you work and tailor prompts accordingly. Keep it false unless you want that behavioral profiling pipeline active.

true.x-description: Activates the profile-pipeline commands (scan-sessions, extract-messages, profile-sample, write-profile, etc.) so GSD can build and use a developer profile. Useful when you want AI behavior tuned to your session patterns.

false.x-description: No developer profiling pipeline commands are available. GSD will not scan or sample your sessions to build a profile.

workflow.ai_integration_phase.x-description: Prompts for an AI-SPEC design contract before planning phases that involve AI systems. When enabled, GSD requires a written design covering model selection, prompts, fallbacks, and evaluation before an AI-related phase can be planned, so architectural tradeoffs are made explicit early. Turn it off if your project does not build AI systems or if you design those systems outside GSD.

true.x-description: Require an AI-SPEC before planning AI system phases. Recommended for any project that builds on top of AI/LLM systems.

false.x-description: Skip the AI-SPEC gate. Use when no phase involves AI systems, or when AI design happens entirely outside GSD.

workflow.api_coverage_gate.x-description: Requires an explicit API-coverage decision before a phase that integrates an external API, SDK, or service can seal. At plan time, the planner is prompted to enumerate the API surface into a COVERAGE.md matrix; at verify time, a blocking gate fails the seal unless the matrix exists and every non-integrated capability is an explicit, reasoned opt-out. This is independent of `workflow.ai_integration_phase` — it applies to any external-API integration, not only AI.

true.x-description: Require an explicit API-coverage matrix (full by default; opt-out must be justified). Recommended — it prevents silently forgetting large parts of an external API.

false.x-description: Skip the API-coverage gate. Use when external API integrations are simple or managed outside this workflow.

workflow.assumption_delta.x-description: Enables the assumption-delta architecture checkpoint during planning. When GSD detects a pluralization, optionality, or chosen/alternative signal in the phase scope, it prompts the planner to re-ask whether the primary key or identity model still names the right thing before the plan is built on top of it. This is advisory only — it never blocks — and helps catch design-rename drift early.

true.x-description: Prompt the planner to re-validate identity-model assumptions when scope signals shift. Recommended — it surfaces naming/design drift without blocking.

false.x-description: Skip the assumption-delta checkpoint. The planner takes the current identity model as given.

workflow.code_review.x-description: Toggles the built-in code review step inside the `/gsd-ship` workflow. When enabled, the ship flow runs a code-review pass against the changes before opening or finalizing a pull request, giving you a structured quality gate before code lands on the base branch. Set it to `false` only if you have a fully separate review process and want ship to skip its own review step.

true.x-description: Run the built-in code-review step as part of `/gsd-ship`. This is the recommended default — it catches common issues before a PR is created.

false.x-description: Skip the built-in code-review step in `/gsd-ship`. Use this only if your project enforces review through external tooling and you do not want GSD's own review pass.

workflow.drift_threshold.x-description: The minimum number of new structural elements (directories, barrel exports, migrations, routes, etc.) that must appear before the codebase drift gate fires its warn or auto-remap action. Raising this reduces noise in fast-growing projects; lowering it makes drift detection more sensitive. This threshold is shared by both the execute-time drift gate and the plan-time precheck.

workflow.nyquist_validation.x-description: Enables Nyquist-inspired validation coverage auditing during the workflow. When on, GSD analyzes your tests and requirements to estimate how well they sample the possible behaviors of the code, and flags areas where coverage is too sparse to give confidence. Turn it off if the coverage-audit noise outweighs its value for a fast-moving project.

true.x-description: Enable Nyquist validation coverage auditing. Recommended — it finds blind spots where your tests are unlikely to catch regressions.

false.x-description: Disable the Nyquist coverage audit. Use only if the reports are routinely ignored or add too much overhead.

workflow.pattern_mapper.x-description: Runs a pattern mapper step before planning when research or other context is available. The pattern mapper looks across your codebase and project signals to surface recurring patterns, conventions, and anti-patterns that the planner should respect, so new work fits the existing design rather than contradicting it.

true.x-description: Run the pattern mapper before planning when context is available. Recommended — it keeps new plans consistent with established project patterns.

false.x-description: Skip the pattern mapper. The planner works only from the direct inputs you give it, without the cross-codebase pattern signal.

workflow.plan_drift_precheck.x-description: Runs a non-blocking codebase-drift check before `/gsd:plan-phase` spawns the planner. If your project's recorded structure (STRUCTURE.md) is stale — meaning directories, routes, or other structural elements have grown beyond `workflow.drift_threshold` — GSD shows an advisory pointing you to `/gsd:map-codebase`. It never blocks planning and never spawns the mapper automatically, so it is safe to leave on in autonomous and CI runs.

true.x-description: Show a plan-time advisory when the codebase structure appears stale. Recommended — it nudges you to refresh STRUCTURE.md without interrupting planning.

false.x-description: Silence the plan-time drift advisory. Keep the execute-time drift gates (`workflow.schema_drift_gate`) enabled separately if you still want those.

workflow.post_planning_gaps.x-description: Runs a post-planning gap report after all plans are generated (plan-phase step 13e). It scans REQUIREMENTS.md and CONTEXT.md decisions against every PLAN.md and prints a unified table showing which items are planned, missing, or only partially covered. This is non-blocking and purely informational — it helps you notice requirements that slipped through the cracks before execution starts.

true.x-description: Run the post-planning gap report. Recommended — it catches requirements and decisions that did not make it into any plan.

false.x-description: Skip the gap report (step 13e). Saves a small amount of time at the end of planning if you do not use the gap table.

workflow.research.x-description: When true, GSD runs a research agent before planning whenever research artifacts are missing or explicitly refreshed. The research agent gathers codebase and domain context so the planner starts from facts rather than assumptions. Keep this on unless you always want to skip the research step and plan directly.

true.x-description: Research runs automatically before planning when needed, building artifacts the planner consumes. Recommended for most projects so plans are grounded in current codebase context.

false.x-description: The research step is skipped. Planning proceeds without a fresh research pass, which is faster but may miss recent context unless research artifacts already exist.

workflow.schema_drift_gate.x-description: Enables the drift gates that run after each execution wave. Two checks happen: a schema-drift gate that blocks verification if schema-relevant files changed but no database push command ran, and a codebase-drift gate that warns when structural additions exceed `workflow.drift_threshold`. Turn both off together only if drift detection routinely fires false positives on your project.

true.x-description: Enable the execute-time drift gates. Recommended — it catches forgotten database pushes and unexpected structural sprawl early.

false.x-description: Disable the execute-time drift gates. Schema changes and structural growth will no longer trigger warnings or blocks.

workflow.schema_push_detection.x-description: Enables ORM schema-push detection during planning. When GSD detects schema-relevant files (migrations, model definitions, ORM config) inside the phase scope, it injects a blocking push task into the plan so the database is migrated as part of execution rather than forgotten. Turn this off only if your project manages database schema entirely outside GSD's awareness.

true.x-description: Detect schema files and inject a blocking push task. Recommended for any project with a database — it prevents 'works on my machine' drift.

false.x-description: Skip schema-push detection. GSD will not add migration tasks automatically, so you must manage them yourself.

workflow.security_asvs_level.x-description: Sets the OWASP ASVS (Application Security Verification Standard) level GSD uses for security review guidance. Level 1 is opportunistic and appropriate for most apps; Level 2 adds standard rigor for apps handling sensitive data; Level 3 is comprehensive and meant for high-assurance, regulated, or high-threat systems. The level scales both how aggressively the planner considers threats and how deeply the auditor verifies mitigations.

1.x-description: Level 1 — opportunistic. A lightweight security baseline suitable for most applications and internal tools.

2.x-description: Level 2 — standard. Adds systematic verification for apps that handle personal or business-sensitive data.

3.x-description: Level 3 — comprehensive. The deepest assurance level, intended for regulated, high-threat, or security-critical systems.

workflow.security_enforcement.x-description: Enables threat-model-anchored security verification through `/gsd-secure-phase`. When on, GSD runs security checks tied to your project's threat model before a phase can advance, using the ASVS level and severity gate configured by the other `workflow.security_*` keys. Turning this off disables security checks entirely — only do that for early prototypes or non-production experiments where security findings would be noise.

true.x-description: Enable threat-model security verification. Recommended for anything beyond throwaway prototypes.

false.x-description: Disable all security enforcement. Threat-model checks are skipped entirely — use only for early experiments or non-production code.

workflow.tdd_mode.x-description: Enables test-driven-development mode for eligible tasks. When on, the planner annotates qualifying tasks with `type:tdd`, and the executor enforces the RED/GREEN/REFRACTOR gate sequence: write a failing test first, make it pass, then refactor. Turn this on when you want TDD discipline applied automatically, and off when you want the planner to choose its own task types.

true.x-description: Enable TDD mode. Eligible tasks follow the RED/GREEN/REFCTOR sequence. Recommended when your team practices TDD and wants the workflow to enforce it.

false.x-description: Disable TDD mode. The planner selects task types normally without forcing the TDD gate sequence.

workflow.ui_phase.x-description: Enables the UI design-contract gate during planning for frontend phases. When on, `/gsd-plan-phase` generates a UI-SPEC.md that captures the visual and interaction contract before implementation begins, so the UI has an agreed-upon design to build against. Turn it off for backend-only projects or phases that have no user interface.

true.x-description: Generate a UI-SPEC.md design contract for frontend phases. Recommended for any project with a user-facing interface.

false.x-description: Skip UI-SPEC generation. Use for backend-only work or when your design process lives entirely outside GSD.

workflow.ui_review.x-description: Enables the retrospective UI audit against implemented frontend code. When on, GSD runs a structured visual and behavioral audit of finished UI work against its UI-SPEC.md contract, catching layout, accessibility, and interaction drift. Turn it off if your project has no UI or you perform UI reviews through another tool.

true.x-description: Run the retrospective UI audit against the UI-SPEC contract. Recommended for frontend work so implemented UI is checked against its design.

false.x-description: Skip the retrospective UI audit. Use when you have no UI-SPEC.md or review UI quality through other means.

workflow.ui_safety_gate.x-description: Blocks planning/execution when a UI-SPEC contract is unmet. Unlike `workflow.ui_phase` (which generates the spec), this key is the enforcement gate: when on, failing to satisfy the UI-SPEC.md prevents the phase from sealing. With both keys on, GSD generates the contract and enforces it — the intended default. Setting `ui_phase:true` and `ui_safety_gate:false` generates a spec in pipelines but does not block manual planning.

true.x-description: Enforce the UI-SPEC contract as a blocking gate. Recommended — unmet UI contracts prevent the phase from advancing.

false.x-description: Do not enforce the UI-SPEC contract. Specs may still be generated by `workflow.ui_phase`, but an unmet spec will never block progress.

workflow.windows_enforce.x-description: Enables the blocking ship-pre gate for the broken-windows ledger (`.planning/WINDOWS.md`). When `true`, `/gsd-ship` blocks while the ledger has any open entry, forcing the team to disposition each tracked deviation before shipping. When `false` (the default), windows are still tracked — the executor and verifier populate the ledger — but ship does not block, letting teams adopt tracking first and enforce later.

true.x-description: Block `/gsd-ship` while any broken-windows ledger entry is open. Opt-in — use once your team is ready for strict enforcement of tracked deviations.

false.x-description: Track broken windows without blocking ship. The ledger is still populated; this is the default so teams can adopt tracking before enforcement.

workflow.agent_hint_routing.x-description: Honors the agent_hint field in a plan's frontmatter by routing that plan to a specific executor agent or model instead of the default. This is a no-op for plans that do not declare an agent_hint, so it is safe to leave on. Keep it on when you occasionally pin a plan to a particular agent, and it has no effect otherwise.

true.x-description: Plans with an agent_hint field are dispatched to the indicated agent or model. Recommended because it is harmless for normal plans and enables opt-in per-plan routing when you need it.

false.x-description: agent_hint frontmatter is ignored and all plans use the default executor. Use this only if you want to guarantee uniform routing and never vary the agent per plan.

phase_commit_docs.x-description: A per-phase override that lets you set commit_docs for a single phase without changing the global default. For example, phase_commit_docs.03 forces a specific behavior just for phase 3. This per-phase value outranks both the explicit config setting and any gitignore auto-detection, so it's the most targeted way to control whether one particular phase's planning is committed.
